readings.title: A group chat with a clear purpose
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: The residents of Linden Court used one chat group for urgent maintenance news, lost umbrellas and long discussions. Important notices were often buried. A volunteer suggested creating a separate announcement channel. Only building notices appeared there, while the original group remained open for conversation. Residents could silence the discussion group without missing a water-supply notice. The volunteer also posted a weekly summary for people who preferred checking less often. The arrangement did not reduce residents' freedom to talk. It made the purpose of each channel clearer and helped people choose how much attention to give it.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Collecting only what an event needs
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An online book club copied a registration form from an earlier outdoor event. The form requested postal addresses and emergency contacts, although participants would now join from home. One organiser asked how each field would be used. The team removed fields unrelated to the online meeting and kept only a name and email address. They explained that the email was needed to send the joining link and a follow-up note. Fewer people abandoned the form. The exercise reminded the organisers that reusing a form also means reconsidering its assumptions, rather than treating every old field as necessary.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: The pause before replying
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: After a difficult meeting, Arun received a short message asking why a task was unfinished. He read it as an accusation and began an angry reply. Before sending it, he reread the original message and realised it contained no criticism of his effort. The sender might simply need a progress update. Arun replied with the current status, the obstacle and a proposed completion time. His colleague thanked him and offered help. The pause did not guarantee agreement, but it allowed him to separate what the message actually said from the intention he had imagined.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A password lesson built around practice
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community digital class once presented a long list of account-safety rules. Learners said they understood, yet many struggled when changing settings at home. The tutor replaced part of the lecture with practice on a demonstration account. Learners located the security menu, compared recovery options and explained the steps to a partner. They never entered real passwords into the shared classroom device. The tutor gave them a short illustrated guide to take home. Questions became more specific, revealing difficulties that a simple request to raise a hand if confused had not uncovered.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
Digital communication asks us to make choices about attention. Not every message deserves an immediate reply, and not every group serves the same purpose. Clear channels and sensible notification settings can help people remain informed without checking their devices constantly. These arrangements work best when members understand which messages are urgent and where they can find a reliable summary of the rest.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 注意not every部分否定与without checking的方式表达。
translation.referenceAnswer: 数字沟通要求我们对注意力的分配作出选择。并非每条消息都值得立即回复，也并非每个群组都有相同的用途。明确的沟通渠道和合理的通知设置，可以帮助人们在不必不断查看设备的情况下掌握信息。当成员清楚哪些消息紧急，以及在哪里能找到其余信息的可靠摘要时，这些安排最能发挥作用。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English to members of a volunteer chat group. Propose rules for separating urgent notices from general discussion, explain the benefits, and invite members to comment.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 清晰区分紧急公告与一般讨论，说明益处并征求反馈。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Dear volunteers,
Our chat group is useful for sharing ideas, but schedule changes can disappear among long conversations. I suggest creating a separate channel for urgent announcements, such as changes to meeting places or session times.
General questions and photographs could remain in the current group. Members would then be free to silence casual discussion during work while keeping important alerts active. An organiser could post a short weekly summary for anyone who prefers to catch up less frequently.
The announcement channel should be used carefully so that ordinary messages are not labelled urgent. Please tell us whether this arrangement would suit your schedule and whether any important information might be missed. We could try it for a month and adjust it together.
Best wishes,
A fellow volunteer
